sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Gradient Boosting (model_id python-gradient-boosting) predicts default.payment.next.month on the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset. Its recorded business purpose, a challenger compared against the production default model that informs but does not drive decisions, was inferred rather than confirmed. This conflicts with the documented limitation that the model is used only for SHAP explainability. The business owner, the intended business use and the decision supported are not documented, and the facts list a risk tier of 2 while also listing the tier/risk rating as missing information.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn GradientBoostingClassifier with random_state set to a seed that defaults to 42 and no other hyperparameters set, so library defaults apply. It uses 21 input features (credit limit, education, marriage, the PAY_0 to PAY_6 repayment-status fields, six bill amounts and six payment amounts); ID, SEX and AGE are excluded from the predictors, though the input feature list itself was inferred. Data is fetched from UCI dataset 350 and validated for shape, missing values and default rate, then split 80/20 into stratified train and test sets with random_state 42 (the train fraction was inferred). No scaling, encoding or class imbalance handling is applied, and no decision threshold is documented.

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: Performance, calibration, fairness, stability and monitoring are not evaluated for this model, since those reports use the Statsmodels candidate, and SHAP explainability is computed only on the first 500 test rows. The model assumes default hyperparameters are adequate, but no rationale for them or any tuning is documented. Training data is public 2005 Taiwanese credit-card demonstration data that is not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio, so its representativeness for any deployment population is unknown. The decision threshold, monitoring plan, approval status and deployment status are not documented.
